target_audience: High School Students and Math Educators

sections.title: The Hook: The 'Confused Architect' Scenario
lecture_lines: Imagine an architect giving vague instructions.
Pip is confused by 'steepness-ish' for his slide.
Without precision, logical structures fall apart.
animations: An architect [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/architect.svg] stands by a table with a messy scribble #A9A9A9 labeled 'Blueprint'.
A penguin (Pip) [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/penguin.svg] stands next to a wavy, dashed line #FF0000 labeled 'steepness-ish?' with a large '?' #FFFFFF.
The wavy line collapses into scattered segments at the bottom of the screen.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The Language of Math
lecture_lines: Effective explanations start with a clear toolbox.
We must define terms like radius and pi.
Establish baseline tools before solving the problem.
animations: A wooden-textured box outline #DEB887 labeled 'Explanation Toolbox' #FFFFFF appears in the center.
Icons for a radius line 'r' #00FFFF, a 'pi' symbol #FFD700, and a square symbol 'x^2' #ADFF2F slide into the box.
The box lid closes and a soft white glow #FFFFFF emanates from its edges.

sections.title: Criterion 1: Visual-Symbolic Mapping
lecture_lines: Never leave equations floating in a vacuum.
Map every symbol to a visual representation.
See (a+b)² as a divided geometric square.
One large square, one small, and two rectangles.
The visual proves the algebra instantly.
animations: The equation '(a+b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2' #FFFFFF appears at the top center.
A large square outline [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg] #FFFFFF appears below the equation.
Two internal lines (one vertical, one horizontal) divide the square into four regions based on segments 'a' and 'b'.
Label the top-left square 'a^2' #FFD700, the bottom-right square 'b^2' #ADFF2F, and the two rectangles 'ab' #1E90FF.
The four region labels #FFD700, #ADFF2F, #1E90FF flash simultaneously and then float up to align with the terms in the equation.

sections.title: Criterion 2: Logical Cohesion (The Chain of 'Why')
lecture_lines: Every step needs a clear 'Because'.
Logical bridges connect each part of the chain.
If one link breaks, the explanation fails.
animations: Three white boxes #FFFFFF labeled 'Step A', 'Step B', and 'Step C' appear horizontally with gaps between them.
Transparent blue arches #1E90FF labeled 'Because' #FFFFFF appear, bridging the gaps between the boxes.
The middle bridge #1E90FF cracks with a red 'X' #FF0000, and the boxes 'Step B' and 'Step C' fall off the screen.

sections.title: Criterion 3: The Principle of Parsimony (Simplicity)
lecture_lines: Use the minimum steps required for rigor.
Avoid heavy jargon when plain language works.
Explain slope as 'up per step right.'
animations: A block of complex text #A9A9A9 regarding 'differential change' appears in a small, cramped font.
A large red 'X' #FF0000 is drawn over the complex text, and it fades away completely.
A simple staircase icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/staircase.svg] #00FFFF appears with arrows showing 'Up' #00FFFF and 'Right' #00FFFF, labeled 'Slope' #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Application: Explaining the Pythagorean Theorem
lecture_lines: Let's apply our criteria to Pythagoras' theorem.
Pip places square crackers around a triangle.
Two small areas fill the largest square.
Like water pouring from small tanks into one.
Logic and visuals combine for a clear proof.
animations: A right-angled triangle #FFFFFF is drawn in the center of the screen.
Three squares are drawn on each side of the triangle: two smaller ones #ADD8E6 and one larger one #FFFFFF.
The two smaller squares #ADD8E6 fill with a blue liquid effect to represent their area.
The blue liquid #ADD8E6 flows from both smaller squares into the largest square, filling it to the brim.
The text 'a^2 + b^2 = c^2' #FFD700 appears below the triangle and glows brightly.

sections.title: The Checklist: Summary & Review
lecture_lines: Review our checklist: Visuals, Logic, and Simplicity.
Test your explanations against these three criteria.
Clear communication makes math accessible for everyone.
animations: A vertical list appears: '1. Visuals', '2. Logic', '3. Simplicity' in white #FFFFFF.
Bright green checkmarks #00FF00 draw themselves next to each item in sequence.
Pip [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pip.svg] #FFFFFF appears at the bottom right, smiling with a green checkmark #00FF00 'stamp' appearing over a clear diagram.
